Treatment summary
Pateint presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with reported head
impact and post-injury symptoms consistent with concussion. Over the course of 11
visits, care focused on symptom monitoring, graded return to daily activities,
vestibular and visual exercises, and headache management. The mechanism and force of
the collision align well with the presenting injury. Treatment extended somewhat
beyond the typical timeline for an uncomplicated concussion, largely because symptoms
improved gradually rather than resolving on a fixed schedule. Several examination
findings, including balance and oculomotor measures, support the diagnosis, while
other neurological screening tests returned within normal limits. The patient reports
no prior injury to the head or neck region, and no earlier treatment for that area is
documented in the records available to this office. Billing records reflect one charge
per scheduled service with no duplicate or repeated entries. Ongoing follow-up is
planned to confirm continued recovery and to address any residual symptoms.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
